events.evidence_text: Nixon married Thelma "Pat" Ryan in 1940.
First daughter Tricia born February 1946.

events.event_description: Elected to US House of Representatives
events.evidence_text: Won California House seat defeating Jerry Voorhis.
Defeated Helen Gahagan Douglas for Senate seat.
Became vice president on Eisenhower ticket.

events.event_description: Lost presidential election to John F. Kennedy
events.evidence_text: Narrowly lost the 1960 presidential race to Kennedy.

events.event_description: Lost California governor race to Pat Brown
events.evidence_text: Defeated for governor; declared it his last press conference.

events.event_description: Elected 37th President of the United States
events.evidence_text: Won 1968 presidential election over Humphrey.
First US president to visit the People's Republic of China.
Won 49 states against McGovern.
Only US president to resign, facing impeachment over Watergate.
Underwent surgery for phlebitis and nearly died from shock.

events.event_description: Suffered major stroke, died four days later
events.evidence_text: Severe stroke at home; died April 22, 1994.

events.event_description: Joined Swiss Patent Office in Bern
events.evidence_text: Hired as technical expert at the federal patent office.
Married fellow physics student Mileva Marić in Bern.
First son Hans Albert born in Bern.

events.event_description: Annus mirabilis papers (photoelectric effect, special relativity, E=mc2)
events.evidence_text: Published four groundbreaking papers in Annalen der Physik.
Second son Eduard born in Zurich.

events.event_description: Moved to Berlin, Prussian Academy of Sciences
events.evidence_text: Accepted Berlin academy post and directorship offer.
Presented final field equations of general relativity.

events.event_description: Physical collapse with liver and stomach illness
events.evidence_text: Fell seriously ill; bedridden for months during wartime.
Divorce from Mileva finalized after years of separation.
Married cousin Elsa months after divorce.

events.event_description: Eclipse observations confirm general relativity; world fame
events.evidence_text: Royal Society announced eclipse results supporting his theory.
Nobel for explanation of photoelectric effect.

events.event_description: Diagnosed with enlarged heart after collapse
events.evidence_text: Collapsed in Switzerland; months of bed rest for heart condition.

events.event_description: Emigrated from Nazi Germany to Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton
events.evidence_text: Left Germany, renounced citizenship, joined Princeton institute.
Operation found aortic aneurysm, later cause of death.
Youngest woman Conservative candidate; lost Dartford to Labour.
Second defeat at Dartford in 1951 election.
Married businessman Denis Thatcher in London.
Gave birth to twins Carol and Mark.
Won Finchley seat in the House of Commons.
Joined Heath cabinet as Secretary of State for Education.

events.event_description: Branded "Thatcher, Milk Snatcher" over school milk cuts
events.evidence_text: Widely criticized for ending free school milk.
Defeated Heath to lead the Conservative Party.

events.event_description: Became first female UK Prime Minister
events.evidence_text: Won general election, first woman prime minister.
Argentine surrender ended Falklands conflict, boosting her standing.
Won large majority in 1983 general election.
Won third term, rare in modern British politics.

events.event_description: Forced to resign after leadership challenge
events.evidence_text: Withdrew from leadership contest and resigned as prime minister.

events.event_description: Series of small strokes; ended public speaking
events.evidence_text: Doctors advised her to stop public speaking after strokes.
Married Janet Shearon in Wilmette, Illinois.
First son Eric born in 1957.
Named in NASA second astronaut group.

events.event_description: Gemini 8: first docking in orbit, then emergency abort
events.evidence_text: Commanded first space docking; safely recovered from thruster malfunction.

events.event_description: First human to walk on the Moon (Apollo 11)
events.evidence_text: Apollo 11 commander, first person on the lunar surface.
Apollo 11 crew honored with Medal of Freedom.

events.event_description: Resigned NASA, became engineering professor at University of Cincinnati
events.evidence_text: Left NASA to teach aerospace engineering in Cincinnati.

events.event_description: Vice chairman of Rogers Commission on Challenger disaster
events.evidence_text: Served as vice chairman of the Challenger investigation commission.
Suffered mild heart attack skiing in Aspen.
Separated in 1990, divorced 1994.
Married Carol Held Knight, met at golf tournament 1992.

events.event_description: Coronary bypass surgery; died of complications
events.evidence_text: Bypass surgery; died August 25, 2012 of complications.

events.event_description: Moved to Paris to study at the Sorbonne
events.evidence_text: Left Warsaw to enroll at the University of Paris.
Married physicist Pierre Curie in Sceaux.
First daughter Irène born, later a Nobel laureate.

events.event_description: Announced discovery of radium (after polonium in July)
events.evidence_text: Curies announced radium discovery to the Academy of Sciences.
First woman awarded a Nobel Prize, for radiation research.
Second daughter Ève born.

events.event_description: Took Pierre's chair: first woman professor at the Sorbonne
events.evidence_text: Appointed to late husband's professorship, first female professor there.

events.event_description: Defeated in election to French Academy of Sciences
events.evidence_text: Lost Academy seat by narrow vote amid hostility.

events.event_description: Press scandal over relationship with Paul Langevin
events.evidence_text: Tabloids attacked her over affair with married physicist Langevin.
Second Nobel, for discovering radium and polonium.

events.event_description: Kidney illness and surgery, depression; withdrew from work
events.evidence_text: Hospitalized late 1911, underwent kidney surgery, months of recovery.

events.event_description: Founded mobile radiology service in WWI; Radium Institute
events.evidence_text: Organized X-ray vehicles for front-line wartime medicine.

events.event_description: Aplastic anemia from radiation exposure; died
events.evidence_text: Died of aplastic anemia linked to radiation exposure.

events.event_description: Moved to Chicago to work as draftsman (Silsbee, then Adler & Sullivan)
events.evidence_text: Began architecture career in Chicago offices.
Married Catherine Tobin in Chicago.

events.event_description: Left Adler & Sullivan over moonlighting; opened own practice
events.evidence_text: Sullivan fired him over private commissions; started own firm.

events.event_description: Abandoned family and practice for Europe with Mamah Borthwick; public scandal
events.evidence_text: Left wife for client's wife, causing major scandal.
Catherine finally granted divorce in 1922.

events.event_description: Imperial Hotel Tokyo survived Great Kanto earthquake
events.evidence_text: His hotel withstood the 1923 earthquake, boosting reputation.
Married sculptor Miriam Noel; marriage failed within a year.

events.event_description: Second Taliesin fire destroyed living quarters
events.evidence_text: Electrical fire destroyed much of Taliesin home.

events.event_description: Arrested with Olgivanna under Mann Act; bank foreclosure on Taliesin
events.evidence_text: Arrested in Minnesota; charges later dropped.
Divorce from Miriam Noel finalized in 1927.
Married Olgivanna in 1928.
Launched apprenticeship program with Olgivanna.
Fallingwater revived career; featured on Time cover.
American Institute of Architects awarded him its Gold Medal.
Married Martin Ginsburg after Cornell graduation.
Daughter Jane born 1955.

events.event_description: Despite top grades, rejected for clerkships and law firm jobs as a woman
events.evidence_text: Turned down for Frankfurter clerkship because she was a woman.
Became professor at Rutgers Law School.
Son James born 1965.

events.event_description: Co-founded ACLU Women's Rights Project; first tenured woman at Columbia Law
events.evidence_text: Led ACLU women's rights litigation and joined Columbia faculty.

events.event_description: Appointed to US Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit
events.evidence_text: Carter appointed her to the D.C. Circuit.

events.event_description: Sworn in as Supreme Court Justice
events.evidence_text: Second woman to serve on the US Supreme Court.
Diagnosed with colon cancer; surgery, chemo, radiation.
Surgery for early-stage pancreatic cancer.

events.event_description: Lung cancer surgery after fall broke ribs
events.evidence_text: Nodules found after rib fracture; lung surgery December 2018.
Court announced completion of radiation for pancreatic tumor.
Announced liver lesions and ongoing chemotherapy.
Married nurse Aletta Louw while practicing in Ceres.

events.event_description: Postgraduate work at University of Minnesota
events.evidence_text: Trained in heart surgery under Wangensteen and Lillehei.
Arthritis diagnosed during postgraduate work in the US.

events.event_description: Returned to Groote Schuur Hospital as head of experimental surgery
events.evidence_text: Appointed head of experimental surgery in Cape Town.

events.event_description: Performed world's first human heart transplant
events.evidence_text: Transplanted heart into Louis Washkansky at Groote Schuur.

events.event_description: First transplant patient died after 18 days
events.evidence_text: Washkansky died of pneumonia eighteen days after surgery.
Fame strained family; divorced in 1969.
Married 19-year-old heiress Barbara Zoellner.
Pioneered heterotopic heart transplant procedure.
Second marriage ended in divorce in 1982.

events.event_description: Retired from surgery due to arthritis
events.evidence_text: Rheumatoid arthritis in hands ended surgical career.

events.event_description: Reputation damaged by endorsing Glycel anti-aging cream
events.evidence_text: Criticized for promoting unproven anti-aging skin cream.
Third marriage, to Karin Setzkorn.
Third marriage ended in divorce in 2000.

events.event_description: Elected first Black president of Harvard Law Review
events.evidence_text: First African American Harvard Law Review president.
Married Michelle Robinson in Chicago.
Won Illinois Senate seat for 13th district.
First daughter Malia born July 1998.

events.event_description: Lost Democratic primary for US House to Bobby Rush
events.evidence_text: Defeated roughly two to one by incumbent Bobby Rush.
Second daughter Sasha born June 2001.

events.event_description: Keynote speech at Democratic National Convention
events.evidence_text: Convention keynote brought national prominence.
Won Senate seat with 70 percent of vote.

events.event_description: Elected 44th President of the United States
events.evidence_text: First African American elected US president.
Nobel committee honored efforts on international diplomacy.
Signed landmark health care reform into law.
Party lost 63 House seats; he called it a shellacking.
Defeated Mitt Romney for second term.

events.event_description: Left office at end of second term
events.evidence_text: Term ended; succeeded by Donald Trump.

events.event_description: Record joint book deal with Penguin Random House
events.evidence_text: Obamas reportedly signed book deal worth over $60 million.

events.event_description: Acted as first lady after mother's death
events.evidence_text: Served as acting first lady for father Park Chung-hee.

events.event_description: Elected to National Assembly in Dalseong by-election
events.evidence_text: Entered parliament in Daegu Dalseong by-election.

events.event_description: Elected chair of Grand National Party
events.evidence_text: Became party leader amid impeachment backlash crisis.

events.event_description: Face slashed by attacker; 60 stitches surgery
events.evidence_text: Attacked with utility knife; 11 cm wound needing surgery.

events.event_description: Lost GNP presidential primary to Lee Myung-bak
events.evidence_text: Narrowly lost party nomination to Lee Myung-bak.

events.event_description: Led Saenuri Party to legislative election win
events.evidence_text: Emergency committee chair; party kept majority.

events.event_description: Elected first female President of South Korea
events.evidence_text: Won presidency over Moon Jae-in.

events.event_description: Heavy criticism over Sewol ferry disaster response
events.evidence_text: Government response to ferry sinking widely condemned.

events.event_description: Impeached by National Assembly over Choi Soon-sil scandal
events.evidence_text: Assembly voted 234 to 56 to impeach her.

events.event_description: Removed from office by Constitutional Court
events.evidence_text: Court unanimously upheld impeachment, first president removed.
Arrested and held in pre-trial detention.

events.event_description: Sentenced to 24 years for corruption and abuse of power
events.evidence_text: Seoul court convicted her on 16 of 18 charges.
Supreme Court upheld retrial sentence, ending legal process.

events.event_description: Pardoned on health grounds; released after hospitalization
events.evidence_text: Moon Jae-in pardoned her citing deteriorating health.
